newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom sees 3 years of dilution from MFS.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom sees 3 years of dilution from MFS.

text.p: WorldCom Inc said Monday it sees three years of earnings per share dilution from its $14 billion acquisition of MFS Communications Co Inc, but expects savings from the takeover to pay for the deal within five to six years.
"Dilution will last maybe three years," Bernard Ebbers chief executive of WorldCom told a news conference here.
"If you look at it on a five to six year basis, it (the savings) more than pays for the transaction," he said.
There were no immediate figures available for the exact per share dilution from 1997 to 1999.

Ebbers said that revenues of the combined company would increase by 30 percent and earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) will increase more than 40 percent in the long term.
The dilution would mainly be from heftier amortization charges, WorldCom officials said.

WorldCom used to have $130 million a year in amortization, but the enlarged company, MFS WorldCom, will have $400 million amortized for the goodwill on MFS' takeover of Uunet, which was completed earlier this month, and $200 million for the goodwill for the takeover of MFS itself.
The shareholders of MFS and the former Uunet shareholders will, after the exercise of all options, own between 55 and 56 percent of the enlarged MFS WorldCom stock.
The two companies have combined debt of $1.3 billion and combined cash of $1.5 billion. -- Nick Louth, New York
